task: Develop a composite risk index combining tropical cyclone regime shifts and sea level rise, applied globally to evaluate mangrove ecosystem risk by end of century.

method_commitments.name: Composite Risk Index (CRI)
method_commitments.definition: CRI = SLR_Risk_Score + TC_Projected_Risk_Score, additive combination of normalized hazard components
method_commitments.range: 0 to 5, mapped to Very Low / Low / Moderate / High / Very High categories
method_commitments.justification: Additive model allows transparent decomposition and avoids multiplicative artifacts when one component is near-zero

method_commitments.name: SLR Risk Component
method_commitments.definition: Based on median RSLR rate for 2080-2100 from IPCC AR6 regional projections. Thresholds from Saintilan et al. (2023): <4 mm/yr (Low), 4-7 mm/yr (Moderate), >=7 mm/yr (High)
method_commitments.data_source: IPCC AR6 sea-level change projections (Garner et al., 2021), SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5

method_commitments.name: TC Risk Component
method_commitments.definition: Baseline TC frequency from MIT historical tracks (1850-2014) combined with regional projected shift factors from Mo et al. (2023) and Kropf et al. (2023). Categories based on Saffir-Simpson scale.
method_commitments.data_source: MIT model downscaled from MPI-ESM1-2-HR (Emanuel et al., 2006)

method_commitments.name: Global Application
method_commitments.definition: Applied to 100,000 sampled mangrove points from Global Mangrove Watch v4 (Bunting et al., 2018)

method_commitments.name: Ecosystem Services Integration
method_commitments.definition: Country-level mangrove area, at-risk population, and beneficiary population from UCSC CWON dataset
method_commitments.purpose: Assess human dimensions of mangrove risk

key_references: Saintilan et al. (2023) - Nature: SLR thresholds for coastal habitat retreat
Mo et al. (2023) - Frontiers in Ecology: TC risk to mangroves
Kropf et al. (2023) - Preprint: Ecosystem vulnerability to TCs
Krauss & Osland (2019) - Annals of Botany: TC effects on mangroves
Dabala et al. (2023) - Nature Communications: Mangrove conservation priorities
limitations: Mangrove data sampled to 10% for computational efficiency
TC shift factors use simplified regional averages rather than grid-cell projections
No dynamic vegetation model; static risk assessment
SLR rates come from medium-confidence regional projections with inherent uncertainty
